purpose: reader-facing explanation of SQLiteSearch's requirements, LSH design, local architecture, and release workflow

required_facts.fact: SQLiteSearch was intended as a persistent local middle ground between in-memory minsearch and infrastructure-heavy search systems.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 15-17 and 85-93: minsearch limitation, project need, and conceptual position are described.

required_facts.fact: The library needed Python availability, easy setup, local execution without Docker, and text plus vector search.
Elasticsearch was described as aimed at large production systems, while Qdrant and PostgreSQL would require external services or Docker in this use case.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 28: alternatives and setup trade-offs are specified.

required_facts.fact: SQLite provided embedded text search and persistent storage but no built-in vector search.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 34-36: SQLite discovery and vector-search limitation are stated.

required_facts.fact: lshashing stored hash tables in memory, SparseLSH lacked SQLite support, and narrow-down used a native Rust extension.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 43-49: candidate limitations are documented.

required_facts.fact: The implementation used locality-sensitive hashing based on random projections familiar to Alexey.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 55: algorithm and rationale are stated.

required_facts.fact: The API was designed to resemble minsearch so Buildcamp participants would not need to learn a new interface.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 57: API compatibility goal is specified.

required_facts.fact: ChatGPT created the plan, Claude Code read plan.md and implemented the library, and tests were requested.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 64-69: plan, repository, implementation, and testing are described.

required_facts.fact: The final index stores data tables, lookup structures, and metadata in one SQLite file and runs without a separate server.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 85-89: single-file architecture and operational properties are stated.

required_facts.fact: A /release command automates PyPI publishing and can rerun after Claude diagnoses build or test failures.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 97-101: release workflow and failure handling are described.

author_attribution: Explain the historical design as documented by Alexey and preserve that SQLiteSearch targets small personal and course projects rather than every production workload.
